source: In the S bus, in the rush hour. A chap of about 26, felt hat with a cord instead of a ribbon, neck too long, as if someone’s been having a tug-of-war with it. People getting off. The chap in question gets annoyed with one of the men standing next to him. He accuses him of jostling him every time anyone goes past. A snivelling tone which is meant to be aggressive. When he sees a vacant seat he throws himself on to it. Two hours later, I meet him in the Cour de Rome, in front of the gare Saint-Lazare. He’s with a friend who’s saying: "You ought to get an extra button put on your overcoat." He shows him where (at the lapels) and why.

In the midst of the bustling supermarket, a cart brimmed with groceries beside the conveyor belt. The cashier scanned items swiftly, her hands moving rhythmically, the beeps of the barcode scanner punctuating the air. Each product zipped past, landing softly in the bagging area, where sturdy plastic bags awaited their contents. A card reader stood to the side, its screen glowing invitingly for the next transaction. The shopper, eyes focused on the array of goods, handed over the card, the machine processing the payment seamlessly.

Behind the current customer, another shopper edged forward, eager to start their own process. The tension was subtle, a minor push against the personal space, a small reminder of the queue's impatience. The cashier, undeterred by the crowd, continued with practiced efficiency. She announced the total with a clear voice, the sound blending with the ambient noise of the store. A prompt for the loyalty card appeared, a familiar request in the retail routine. The shopper, slightly flustered by the pressure, fumbled through their wallet, eventually producing the card.

The cashier’s smile, warm and professional, eased the momentary friction. The receipt printer whirred, the paper spooling out neatly, a final record of the transaction. Another cart was pushed forward, the divider bar marking the transition between customers. The conveyor belt started anew, the cycle repeating with seamless precision. Behind, the impatient shopper sighed, the queue inching forward, the routine of the checkout line continuing unabated.

Each beep marked progress, the total called out clear and firm. Loyalty cards were proffered, transactions sealed. In the narrow confines, elbows clashed, a subtle dance of irritation. Yet, the rhythm of commerce continued, unyielding and constant.
